messages:
Anya: Heads-up — I'm going to propose a "surgical" cutover approach for tenant-level residency enforcement tonight. Not a full handoff, just a scoped route tweak for a small tenant slice to validate legal routing + fallback behavior. Thoughts? :scalpel:

Devon: +1 to scoped. can we limit to read-only traffic first? safer to measure routing headers and rx path before write experiments.

Sam: Read-only probe seems good. Also recommend an automated rollback window (5m) if resident_write_errors or fallback_rate go above threshold.

Maria: Quick checklist: 1) patch proxy to set X-Region-Policy = "surgical-v1" 2) wire telemetry for `resident_write_errors`, `fallback_latency_p50/p95`, `route-accept-rate` 3) precreate alert runbook.

Anya: Exactly. Plan: deploy proxy rule on canary infra, run 10k read requests with header `X-Region-Policy: surgical-v1` for tenant t-1042, then flip a write-simulation that intentionally targets resident-only path but with fallback enabled.

Lee: operator note — make sure KV-cache TTL is zeroed for that tenant so we don't mask routing effects. otherwise prefix caching will hide the routing change.

Sam: Good call. Also add an idempotency token pattern so we can dedupe writes if rollback happens.

Devon: Sample curl to simulate header for test traffic:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN"
       -H "X-Region-Policy: surgical-v1"
       -d '{"tenant":"t-1042","input":"probe"}'
       https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate > /dev/null &
 done
wait
```

Maria: ops-bot will post canary metrics once the deploy happens. I can own alerts + runbook. Who's on-call for rollback?

Anya: Sam will be primary rollback owner, Lee is secondary. If `resident_write_errors` > 0.5% for 2m OR `fallback_latency_p95` increases by >300ms baseline, we revert proxy rule.

ops-bot: Deploy queued: `proxy-rule/surgical-v1` -> canary cluster in staging (ID 7852). Watch: https://observability.local/canary/7852 :rocket:

Sam: I want an explicit stubbed fallback test that simulates third-party throttle — ensure fallback path doesn't escalate to global-write-route unexpectedly.

Devon: Another safety: add a header `X-Policy-Debug: true` in canary so datastore logs include the policy decision for each request — makes post-mortem trivial.

Anya: Good. Post-checks to run after 10k reads + 1k simulated writes: export `route.decisions`, `kv.cache_hits_by_tenant`, `latency.p95` and sanity-check PII counters. If all green, we can roll to 10% of tenant traffic tomorrow.

Maria: I'll draft the runbook now and attach thresholds. ping me in #eng-oncall when you want go/no-go.

Sam: One long-term thought — if the surgical pattern works we should codify a lightweight "traffic-scalpel" primitive in the proxy so PMs can request tiny scoped changes without an operator dance. But for tonight we do it manual.

Anya: Agreed. Thanks team. I'll start the patch and open the PR with `ops-bot` link.

arch-team-bot: Note: remember to include consent audit header for EU tenants when enabling residency enforcement. See RFC-223 for header format.

Lee: quick reminder — update tenant policy metadata store so simulated requests reflect the resident region flag; otherwise the control plane will override.

Anya: Copy. I'll post the PR and timeline here when ready. :hourglass:
